chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A young man was brought to Ali (peace be upon him) in whom there was doubt regarding whether he had reached puberty (via wet dream), so he cut off the tips of his fingers.

key_terms.احْتِلَام: Wet dream, sign of reaching puberty

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a boy whose puberty status is uncertain in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This incident from al-Isfahani highlights the juristic principle of *ihtiyat* (caution) in applying *hadd* punishments when the condition of puberty (*bulugh*) is ambiguous. By cutting the finger tips rather than the entire hand, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) demonstrated a flexible application of the theft penalty, balancing the severity of the punishment with the uncertainty of the boy's legal maturity. This narration is frequently cited by Shia jurists to discuss the threshold of criminal responsibility and the gradation of penalties for minors.
